notes:
Four bullets, three steps, all on one NPC in one zone. Bullet 4 is the mini-game's timing instruction and belongs to the conversation bullet 3 opens -- you walk nowhere between them and 'wait ten seconds, then select Push!' is not a rung anyone can be tracked through -- so 3 and 4 merge and the counting advice becomes a note. The requested item is ONE OF FOURTEEN, picked at random per player, and items_alt cannot say that: it means items OR any one of items_alt, so listing the fourteen there would light the marker for a player holding nothing but a Sunsand. Only the Kindred's Crest is recorded, items_partial is set, and the fourteen are named in the step note. The ten merit points are invisible to the addon; so is which item you were asked for. Nothing here carries evidence -- the [KI] Soul gem is the reward, which proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done. 'Nomad Moogle' is one of the known ambiguous names (every Nomad Moogle in Vana'diel folds to one key), which is why all three steps keep their zone. The References section holds one forum link and no steps.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: items_partial is set because that AND-of-an-OR has no slot here.

steps.note: he names which of the fourteen items he wants; the choice is random and nothing in the packets reports it

The Crest AND the one item he asked for, with 10 merit points banked. The fourteen possibilities are Sunsand, Magicked Skull, Damselfly Worm, Crab Apron, Bloody Robe, Dhalmel Saliva, Wild Rabbit Tail, Orcish Axe, Faded Crystal, Yagudo Caulk, Orcish Armor Plate, Quadav Backscale, Dangruf Stone, Siren's Tear Crests also come from Login Campaign points at 5 apiece, or from Shemo at 3:1 from any other seal.

the mini-game. Wait ten seconds after he says to start, then pick 'Push!'. Each '...' is one second and he only counts to four, so keep the pace yourself; the close-up of your own character is the other cue. Too fast or too slow and you simply repeat it.

The step that starts the quest is the UNNUMBERED lead-in sentence above bullet 1, not bullet 1, so step 1 carries an empty source_bullets and says so. Bullets 1 to 3 are one action: go to the tree, open the coffer, receive the gauntlets -- the travel adds no marker the coffer step does not already carry. The coffer is a genuine expressible OR: the header names Boyahda Coffer Key -OR- Thief's Tools, so items_alt holds the tools rather than falling back on items_partial. The page writes only 'the coffer' and never names the object; STAGE D removed the 'Treasure Coffer' name the draft had borrowed from the sister page Borghertz's Striking Hands, because a name must appear in THIS page's text. The coffer step keeps its rung, its zone and its Old gauntlets evidence but carries no marker, and it is demoted to medium. Bullet 5 is conditional on this being your first artifact quest, so both of its sub-bullets are optional steps rather than ladder positions; the 1,000 gil is a note because gil is not an inventory item the addon can see. Bullet 10 is a kill AND an examine and splits accordingly, which is the whole reason the torch is visited twice. The ??? in Port Jeuno is an object and can never carry a marker, but it keeps its rung and its zone, and the quest ends on it -- there is no hand-in NPC. The 'Two Additional Coffers' section is not steps: the page says outright that they are not required and that the quest is completed once you have the hands.

notes:
A clean seven-rung ladder. The two unnumbered 'Notice:' lines are not steps: the first is a precondition (wait one game day and re-zone after Fires of Discontent) that nothing in the packets can observe, the second is inventory advice about the final cutscene. Bullet 8 is the reward landing, an outcome rather than an action. Bullet 3 is one step and not two -- speak to Blatherix and trade him in the same breath, and consecutive rungs on one NPC are one marker anyway; his price is 30 Gob. Chocolate OR 5,000 gil, and gil has no expression here, so items_partial carries the branch. The Mine shaft key is the quest's only observable: it is granted at bullet 3 and that is where the evidence sits. The page never actually says what the key is FOR -- bullet 5 has you examine the Corroded Door with no mention of it -- so it is deliberately not recorded as a requirement on that step; asserting a hold the page does not state would be guessing. The battlefield's own zone is never named either; since the door is in Pashhow Marshlands (S) and the page says clearing it returns you there, the fight keeps that zone rather than going placeless.

notes: Six steps, five of them on three objects in one zone, and the whole quest never has you speak to a single NPC. The header's giver Excenmille is kept as the start because he is a real standing entity in Xarcabard (S) and the walkthrough does not contradict him -- it simply never mentions him until he turns up as your ally in the battlefield -- but the first thing a player actually does is examine the Animal Spoor, so the flag records the disagreement rather than hiding it. Bullets 1 to 3 are three separate examines and not one: the Animal Spoor is visited twice with the Wheel Rut in between, and it is the SECOND visit that grants the Vial of military prism powder, which is this quest's only observable. The Vial is recorded as a hold on the portal step: the page does not say so outright, but it says that losing the battlefield means waiting a day and returning to the Animal Spoor for ANOTHER vial, which only makes sense if entering consumes it. Bullet 4 is one step, not two -- the first examine is a cutscene and the second is the same click on the same door. Bullets 5 and 6 are the battle: Excenmille's assist, his Stag's Cry and Songbird Swoop, the kiting and sleep strategy and Invincible are all commentary on one fight, and the unnumbered line above them is where the roster is actually written. The last instruction -- examine the Wheel Rut again for the closing cutscene -- is an UNNUMBERED paragraph after bullet 6, so its step carries empty source_bullets. 'If you are working on missions then return to Fate in Haze' belongs to a mission, not here. The battlefield's own zone is never named; Xarcabard (S) is kept because the page says to examine the Wheel Rut 'back at (I-9)' afterwards.

notes:
The third Borghertz's Hands page in this batch and the same ladder as the other two, sharing Crawler's Nest and the Nest Coffer Key with Borghertz's Striking Hands and Beastmaster in place of Monk. Two things differ from its siblings and both are worth recording. First, bullet 10 here says to examine the SAME torch you used to spawn Dark Spark, where the other two say 'one of the torches'; this page is the more specific and it costs nothing to follow. Second, the header says 'Repeatable: Yes' and the page carries Category:Repeatable Quests, while the two sister pages say 'Repeatable: af' for the identical quest shape -- an artifact-armour category leaking into the field, which means no. Beast Gloves are a one-time artifact reward, so the field is recorded as false against the header; getting it wrong the other way would leave the marker up forever on a finished quest. The quest starts on the unnumbered lead-in sentence rather than bullet 1, so step 1 has empty source_bullets; the header omits Guslam's grid and the lead-in supplies (H-8). The coffer OR-branch is expressible from the header (Nest Coffer Key -OR- Thief's Tools) and goes in items_alt. STAGE D: unlike Borghertz's Striking Hands, whose bullet 1 says 'find a Treasure Coffer', this page never names the coffer -- bullet 1 is just 'Go to Crawler's Nest' -- so the borrowed name is removed and the coffer step is unmarkable and medium. STAGE D also demotes the quest to medium: keeping repeatable false is almost certainly right for a one-time artifact reward, but it overrides an explicit 'Repeatable: Yes' header plus Category:Repeatable Quests on the strength of the two sister pages rather than on anything this page says, and that override deserves to be visible. Bullet 5's two sub-bullets are conditional on this being your first artifact quest, so they are optional. Bullet 10 is a kill and an examine and splits. The 'Two Additional Coffers' section is all sub-bullets with no numbering, is explicitly not required, and is not steps.
